title: TIDAL: Temporally Interleaved Diffusion and Action Loop for High-Frequency VLA Control
abstract: arXiv:2601.14945v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large-scale Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer semantic generalization but suffer from high inference latency because they adopt a low-frequency batch-and-execute paradigm. This frequency mismatch creates an execution blind spot, causing failures in dynamic environments where targets move during the open-loop execution window. We propose TIDAL (Temporally Interleaved Diffusion and Action Loop), a hierarchical framework that decouples semantic reasoning from high-frequency actuation. TIDAL operates as a backbone-agnostic scheduler for diffusion-based VLAs, using a dual-frequency architecture to redistribute the computational budget. Specifically, a low-frequency macro-intent loop caches semantic embeddings, while a high-frequency micro-control loop interleaves single-step flow integration with execution, conditioning on the latest state fused with motion cues. translated_abstract: 大规模视觉-语言-动作模型具备语义泛化能力，但由于采用低频的“批量生成-执行”范式而面临高推理延迟问题。这种频率失配造成了执行盲区，导致在目标于开环执行窗口内发生移动的动态环境中出现失败。我们提出了TIDAL（时间交错扩散与动作循环），这是一种将语义推理与高频执行解耦的分层框架。TIDAL作为基于扩散模型的VLA的骨干无关调度器运行，利用双频架构重新分配计算预算。具体而言，低频宏观意图循环缓存语义嵌入，而高频微观控制循环将单步流积分与执行交错进行，并以融合运动线索的最新状态作为条件。为应对由此产生的延迟偏移，我们引入了一种时间（注：原摘要在此处截断）
tldr: TIDAL提出了一种骨干无关的双频分层调度框架，通过低频宏观意图循环缓存语义嵌入、高频微观控制循环将单步流积分与执行交错进行，解决了VLA模型因低频批处理范式导致的高推理延迟及其在动态环境中造成的执行盲区问题。
en_tdlr: TIDAL is a backbone-agnostic dual-frequency hierarchical framework that decouples semantic reasoning from high-frequency actuation by interleaving single-step flow integration with execution in a micro-control loop, overcoming the execution blind spot caused by high inference latency in diffusion-based VLA models.
